- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent price is falling.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points in 3-5 days), especially if sentiment is neutral or positive — cap forecast at 1-2% below peak or use moving average to smooth.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 10-15% unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.
- Horizon-specific: 10-15 day forecasts often overestimate; 20+ day forecasts underperform — adjust downward for longer horizons if sentiment is weak or neutral.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to catch the reversal — add a “sentiment pivot” rule: if sentiment >0.67 at day 10+ of forecast, reduce forecast by 1-3% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
